transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-18 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE, brief), Lena Ortiz (CISO, Acme Health), Dr. Rajiv Menon (Head of AI), Tara Hughes (Legal), Omar Ruiz (Platform Ops)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining uh glad we could align schedules, we're here to run through security, privacy and specifically data handling -- prompt retention, PHI questions, and the usual SOC2/ISO stuff. lena, do you want to kick off with your main concerns?

[00:18] Lena Ortiz: thanks maya, yeah main thing for us is understanding exactly what is retained by default at the hosted api level; whether prompts or generated content are stored, for how long, and importantly whether anything could be used to improve models - we cannot have PHI leaking into training sets. also we need details on encryption at rest and customer key mgmt, and audit logs for access review.

[00:40] Samir Patel: sure, i can walk through our typical hosted flow. by default requests hit the hosted api, we surface logs and metrics, and there's a retention window configurable. i want to say default short-term retention is 30 days for logs and 90 days for prompt/content for troubleshooting, but there're options to disable retention or move to Dedicated/Private where retention is under your control. i'll clarify the exact defaults in the artifacts we send.

[01:05] Dr. Rajiv Menon: quick clarifying q - when you say 'no training' is that a contractual guarantee or an operational policy? we need legal language for contracts.

[01:15] Maya Chen: great question. short answer: we do not use customer content to train our base models. that's both an operational policy and we can provide written confirmation. for hosted customers, we offer options: opt-out of retention, dedicated pools, or private deployment. for PHI workflows we typically recommend dedicated or private plus a BAA. tara, any legal framing?

[01:40] Tara Hughes: yes we need the wording and evidence - SOC 2 controls mapping that covers data segregation and training restrictions, plus a BAA for PHI. also need details on who within Redwood can access raw prompts - engineered access, breakglass procedures, etc.

[01:58] Samir Patel: access is RBAC-driven; we authenticate via SSO/SAML and we have role tiers: support, infra, sec, and dev. support access to raw content is scoped and logged; there's a breakglass cadence for incident response and requires approval from security + audit trail. all such events are visible in audit logs.

[02:20] Omar Ruiz: what's the granularity of the audit logs? we need to show who viewed content and timestamps, ideally immutable logs that can be exported to our SIEM.

[02:30] Samir Patel: logs capture user id, role, action (read/write/admin), resource id, timestamps, request metadata and IPs; we can stream audit logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export for retention beyond our UI. we'll include sample schema in the follow-up.

[02:55] Lena Ortiz: on encryption - can you explain key management? do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) in KMS or HSM?

[03:05] Samir Patel: yes, we support customer-managed KMS keys in our Private offering, and for Dedicated we can integrate with your cloud KMS to encrypt model artifacts and content at rest. hosted API supports envelope encryption with our keys, and for customers with strict requirements we recommend Private or a VPC deployment with BYOK (bring your own key).

[03:30] Dr. Rajiv Menon: ok follow-up - if we go hosted, and retain prompts for 90 days, is there any automated redaction or PII detection? we have lots of PHI and would like configurable redaction prior to storage.

[03:45] Samir Patel: we have a PII detection pipeline that can optionally redact or token mask content at ingestion; it's configurable via rules. for PHI specifically we recommend preprocessing on your side or using our redaction layer in front of the api. that's another reason customers choose dedicated/private - more control and no default retention.

[04:05] Tara Hughes: and the BAA question - do you currently sign BAAs for customers handling PHI?

[04:12] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood has a standard BAA we can execute. we do have customers in healthcare under BAA and we can share redacted copies of current BAAs and the process. we'll send you the template.

[04:28] Lena Ortiz: can you confirm controls around 'no training on customer data'? i need to understand exceptions - e.g., aggregated telemetry, system-level logs, or synthetic data.

[04:40] Samir Patel: operationally we separate telemetry from customer content. telemetry (metrics, anonymized latencies) may be used to improve platform performance, but raw prompts and outputs are not used to train our foundation models. that is documented in our privacy policy and is part of our SOC 2 & ISO artefacts. we'll provide a signed statement for contracts. exceptions: aggregated, de-identified stats only. no raw content ingestion into training pipelines.

[05:05] Dr. Rajiv Menon: do you have an internal product for model fine-tuning for customers that want private fine-tunes? is that ever done on customer content?

[05:16] Samir Patel: we support private fine-tuning in Dedicated/Private for customers who opt-in; that's strictly opt-in and happens in isolated environments, and the customer retains control over datasets and keys. we don't automatically fine-tune on hosted customer traffic.

[05:33] Maya Chen: i'll highlight that in the follow-up: hosted = no training; private/dedicated = customer-controlled fine-tune if requested.

[05:45] Tara Hughes: auditability is critical. can you provide evidence for SOC2 controls around change management and access reviews? we need help mapping controls for our vendor risk team.

[05:56] Samir Patel: yes we can send the SOC 2 Type II report and a high-level controls mapping. we also have ISO 27001 and other attestations; samir to attach the evidence pack.

[06:12] Lena Ortiz: data residency - our data residency requirement: EU-only storage for EU patient data. can Redwood restrict data to eu-west?

[06:22] Samir Patel: yes, we support regional data residency. hosted routes can be pinned to region (e.g., eu-west-1), and Dedicated/Private gives full control. we'll provide region routing docs and how to pin keys and logs to region.

[06:38] Omar Ruiz: retention windows again - you mentioned defaults, but we need a hard limit. can we set retention to zero for prompts in hosted, i.e., ephemeral mode?

[06:47] Samir Patel: yes, ephemeral mode is supported: no storage of prompts or outputs, only ephemeral compute; but note it may limit some debugging capabilities. for strict PHI use, ephemeral or Private is recommended.

[07:00] Lena Ortiz: instrumenting SSO will be required - we use Okta. how is SAML implemented and what about SCIM for provisioning?

[07:08] Samir Patel: we support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. roles map to RBAC policies and we can send the SSO config guide.

[07:22] Tara Hughes: who would sign the BAA on Redwood side? legal? do you have a turnaround time?

[07:28] Maya Chen: our legal team executes BAAs; typical turnaround once terms are agreed is 1-2 weeks. we'll attach a template to speed review.

[07:40] Dr. Rajiv Menon: one more technical: are prompts stored in plaintext at rest before encryption? we need guarantees of encryption-in-transit and at-rest and that keys are rotated.

[07:52] Samir Patel: TLS v1.2+ in transit, at-rest encrypted with AES-256 and envelope encryption. key rotation is supported; if you use CMK in Private we don't have key material. we will provide KMS integration docs.

[08:07] Lena Ortiz: any chance of deriving downstream model outputs being linked back to specific patient prompts? this is a risk for re-identification.

[08:20] Samir Patel: we take measures: isolation, access controls, and redaction tools. but re-identification risk is a function of data and model behavior; we recommend preprocessing and PII removal for PHI sensitive content and using dedicated/private infra for higher assurance.

[08:38] Maya Chen: maybe helpful to summarize options: 1) Hosted with ephemeral/no retention + opt-out + SAML/SCIM + BAA; 2) Hosted with retention configurable and PII redaction layer; 3) Dedicated reserved capacity with stricter controls and customer KMS + streaming logs; 4) Private on-prem/VPC deployment with full control and BAA.

[09:02] Tara Hughes: sounds good. please include example contractual language on 'no training' and the exceptions for aggregated telemetry.

[09:12] Maya Chen: absolutely. we'll provide a written confirmation and the SOC 2 artifacts. samir will send logs schema. legal will circulate BAA.

[09:24] Jordan Lee: quick note - in Dedicated we can also do network egress filtering and private networking so logs never leave the VPC unless you want.

[09:33] Omar Ruiz: ok last item - incident response: if there's a data leak how are customers notified and what is the SLA?

[09:42] Samir Patel: we have incident response playbooks, 24/7 on-call for critical incidents, and contractual breach notification timelines in our standard contract (we notify within 72 hours for security incidents affecting customer data); we can provide the IR summary.

[09:58] Lena Ortiz: good. we'll need to review all artifacts and then set follow-up to technical deep-dive to validate config.

[10:05] Maya Chen: great, we'll send docs and propose a technical deep dive week of 3/23. any final q's?

[10:12] Dr. Rajiv Menon: none from me, but please include the redaction and PII detection notes.

[10:20] Tara Hughes: no further q's, thank you.

[10:24] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, recap of next steps - i'll email SOC2/ISO, samir will share logs and encryption/KMS docs, legal will send BAA. we'll set the deep dive.

Meeting end.
